pr_body:
Settings search used to work only on properties, so if a searchbox text
was a substring of a category but not of a property the whole category
would be filtered out and no property would be shown.

Now the behaviour is changed so that when the searchbox text is a
substring of a category all its properties are shown too.

The previous behaviour is still present so that in case the searchbox
text is both a substring of a category and a property of another
category, all properties of the first category are shown and only the
property of the second category is shown.

Fixes #33005

![settings-search](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/3314350/67521388-4be1da80-f69a-11e9-864e-c66f260a53b2.gif)

issue_context.title: Project Settings search brings weird results
issue_context.body:
**Godot version:**
3.2 alpha-2

**OS/device including version:**
OSX Sierra

**Issue description:**
When searching in the project settings to filter elements, the displaying results behave strangely. For example if I search for 'window', when I type 'wi' it appears, and then if I type 'win' it doesn't appear anymore. I've tried this for other settings and I don't really understand the results, seems to behave randomly to me.

**Steps to reproduce:**
In any project, open Project Settings and search for a setting by typing the first letter, then the second then the third and so on, and see how search results behave.

**Minimal reproduction project:**
Empty new project.
comments: It's searching for property name only (not the category), `window` is showing for `wi` because there's `width` and `test_width` properties within this category.
Oh I see now, my bad for not noticing this. In this case what's the way to search only for categories ? Thanks.
It'd probably make sense to search in category names as well. This always throws me off when searching for "stretch mode" or "stretch aspect" :slightly_smiling_face:
It was change in #30516, previously (in 3.1.1) it was searching by full property name.
What would be the expected behaviour here? If I search `Application` should I see just the category and its subcategories? Or should I also see all its subcategories' properties?

> It was change in #30516, previously (in 3.1.1) it was searching by full property name.

Ah right, I had missed that change. The previous behaviour should be brought back.

> What would be the expected behaviour here? If I search `Application` should I see just the category and its subcategories? Or should I also see all its subcategories' properties?

IMO it should list all properties which contain the filter, whether it's in the property name itself or further up its path (i.e. a category/sub-category). So yeah if you search `Application` it should show all subcategories and properties in that category.
Ok seems better to me, the actual state is quite confusing.
can someone add a "regression" label to this issue thanks

review_comments: I wonder why this is needed? The previous code was already checking if the `filter` is either in the property name or the rest of its path (`cat`), so here it should have been working fine?
`cat` here was always an empty `String`, probably there's an issue somewhere else?
Judging by the code, it's not meant to be empty, otherwise there wouldn't be a point in testing it. So yeah, would be worth investigating deeper.

Seems like when the `EditorInspector` is used in the engine Inspector `cat` is correctly set and `property_prefix` is empty, viceversa when it's used either in the project or editor settings.

Those variable are deduced from the `EditorInspector`'s property list on [line 1463](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/33047/files/b03f5bb99d409cb5f369d04e08ba0541e6538cba#diff-554c9c97362d5a6f63b7244253542ffeL1463) and it has been this way since [`005b69cf6e`](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/commit/005b69cf6e276209464cc8c36ebc7376679925b6) when `editor_inspector.h/cpp` have been created, so my guess is that it's expected to be like so. Don't know if I'm missing something.
